title: Dementus: Character Analysis [Fury Road & Furiosa Spoilers]

commenti.body:
I was confused by the inconsistency of Dementus' character at first. At the start of the movie, he appears like an almost majestic holy figure. Then we see him as someone cruel. Then lastly as goofy and a complete failure. Immortan Joe makes a joke out of him by showing how futile his pathetic attempts are to try and inspire an uprising in his Warboys, who are so loyal to him that they would gladly die for him. We also see how he completely fails to rule over anything, with Gastown and the Bulletfarm devolving into chaos. And towards the end of the film there are not much people left to follow him. He seems like a rather pathetic villain in the end.

And I think the inconsistency of his character may be due to us seeing him through the eyes of Furiosa. As a child, perhaps he seems intimidating to her. When he executes her mother, he seems even cruel. But as an adult, he seems pathetic to her. And she understands that her vengeance won't give her any joy, as he is not the imposing villain he seemed when she was young.

I wasn't a huge fan of Furiosa but Dementus was my favorite thing about it for a couple reasons

yes, Hemsworth is hamming it up, but I think that added a lot of balance to the bleakness of all of the other characters. He's the parallel of the "guitar guy" from Fury Road...goofy and intimidating simultaneously

now, as a character, I understand what you're saying and agree with it but I'm gonna make reference two other works: firstly, Game of Thrones. I'm rewatching GOT (not excited to get to season 5+ but whatever, seasons 1-4 are impeccable) and in season 4, when Tywin has his first convo with Tommen post-Joffrey's death, Tywin says this about King Robert: "a man who thinks winning and ruling are the same thing". Then, I'm also reminded of the Dark Knight when the Joker talks about him being like a dog that's chasing cars...he doesn't know what he would do if he actually caught a car

both of those help to describe the nuance of Dementus to me. He's a very charismatic leader...he's physically strong (which of course is important in an uncivilized world), a great talker and knows how to keep his gang happy. But he's a shit ruler because all he knows is how to rape and pillage.

he's really the only character of Furiosa that has any dimension. Every other character is kind of summed up by one or two words, even Furiosa. But Dementus is complex and very enjoyable imo

I just didn't enjoy many other parts of the movie

I see Dementus as very much a foil to Max - what Max could have become if he really did go mad and lose his humanity. The backstory - that Dementus lost his wife and child - is pretty much identical to Max's. But Max became a loner "just trying to survive" - one who can't help but occasionally help people. Dementus went the opposite way, someone who surrounds himself with people, talks a big game about helping the little guy (he spends the whole movie spouting a bunch of socialist rhetoric that he's incapable of delivering on). 

At his core, I think he wants to bring other people, like Furiosa, down to his level. He wants other people to suffer the thing he's suffered and lose the things he's lost. He can't stand that Furiosa had a family that loved her and then found someone else who genuinely cares for her. He hopes that by killing everyone she loves, he can turn her into a new version of himself - a kind of an heir. But Furiosa is holding onto that seed of hope - quite literally, she wears it in her hair - no matter what he puts her through.

I think yall are taking the "Dementus wanted to prepare her" thing as way more than it is: a pathetic narcissist begging for his life, willing to say anything to try and save his life. He never gave a shit about her apart from "appearing fatherly".
in a cruel apocalyptic world, only the people in power are able to have any sort of personality or life. everyone else is just barely surviving.

I think you misunderstood my comment. I don't think he wanted to "prepare" her for the horrors of the world - I think that's a BS line that he spouts to justify his own crap. But I do think he wanted her to suffer the way he had; he can't stand the idea of other people being happy or having a family.
